title: 1. Article 1 – Name and Territory of India

blocks.content:
Article 1 states:

“India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.”



IMPORTANT POINTS:

• India is called both **India** and **Bharat** in the Constitution.

• The word **Union** was chosen deliberately.



WHY ‘UNION’ AND NOT ‘FEDERATION’?

• Indian federation is NOT the result of an agreement among states.

• States cannot secede from the Union.

• The Union is indestructible, but states can be reorganized.



EXAM TRAP:

Q. India is described as what in Article 1?

✔ Union of States
India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.

rows: Includes States, Union Territories, and Acquired Territories
Members share federal power with the Centre
Includes entities directly administered by the Central Government

items: Difference between 'Union of India' (States only) and 'Territory of India' (States + UTs + Acquired Territories) is frequently asked in Polity prelims.
Remember that the Indian federation is not based on an agreement among states, unlike the American federation.
Foreign territories can be acquired by India according to modes recognized by international law (cession, occupation, conquest, or subjugation).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 1 describes India, that is Bharat, as a 'Union of States' rather than a 'Federation of States'.
The phrase 'Territory of India' is a wider expression than 'Union of India' because it includes States, Union Territories, and territories that may be acquired.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar noted that 'Union of States' was preferred to indicate that the federation is not the result of an agreement and no state has the right to secede.
The country is an indestructible Union of destructible states, granting Parliament authority to redraw administrative boundaries.
